The step definitions for supervision r184, r185 and r186 are written, and all of w243's scenarios now pass. I changed no production code, because the code behind these three requirements already existed.

- **Red:** `python3 -m pytest -q --work-item w243` first showed 4 failures, all from missing step definitions.
- **Green:** the same command now gives 185 passed, 1 skipped. Running `tests/scenarios/test_supervision.py` alone gives 4 passed.
- **Size check:** `tools size --limit 300` printed nothing. I did not run the whole suite; the brief's record shows 1086 passed and 5 failed at the start, 4 of them this work-item's scenarios.
- **r186:** the Then step now accepts an optional "for p1", so the deprecated r149 wording still binds to the same step.
- **r185:** the Given step now turns "an empty file set" into an empty file set for the stand-in researcher. I added a Then asserting that no question naming the file set as missing was written.
- **r184:** the new module `tests/scenarios/supervision_awaiting_steps.py` holds the Givens and Thens for p1 and w2. The Givens write the answered question first in `## Questions`, so the single answer lines up with it by position. A one-line import of the new module is added to `tests/scenarios/test_supervision.py`.

Two cases the scenarios don't cover, left as they are: if a node is printed twice in one run, the r184 Thens read only its first printing. The r185 Then treats any question holding both "file set" and "missing" as naming the file set.

The work is one commit, `8f8b2d2e`. The report is `.shop/scratch/3-implement/report.md`, and the result file says `DONE`.
